title: Fpqc covers remain fpqc after canonical universe enlargement
statement: Let $X$ and $U_i$ be schemes in universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme], indexed by $I$ in universe $u+1$, and let $f_i:U_i\to X$ be an fpqc covering family [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The family of canonical enlarged maps $f_i^{\uparrow}:U_i^{\uparrow}\to X^{\uparrow}$ [def-trf-scheme-universe-enlargement] is an fpqc covering. There is no quasi-compactness assumption on individual $f_i$, and an empty covering family of the empty base is allowed.

source.place: Section fpqc (Tag 022B), definition-fpqc-covering and lemma-recognize-fpqc-covering; canonical affine gluing of schemes.tex Section glueing-schemes (Tag 01JA); Bhatt-Scholze Definition 4.1.1.

proof.text: On each affine chart the enlargement replaces the coordinate ring A by ULift A. The prime-spectrum homeomorphism and transported localization maps identify affine opens and images; flatness is invariant under these ring equivalences. The affine-colimit leg equations identify the resulting chart morphisms with the canonical lifted morphisms.

For each affine open in the original base take the finite affine refinement supplied by the fpqc hypothesis. Transport the finitely many source opens and their union of images to the corresponding enlarged affine base chart. The affine recognition criterion for an fpqc covering gives the condition over the enlarged base. The union also gives joint surjectivity. Empty families and arbitrary index sets use the same finite-refinement condition.

lean.statement:
theorem fpqc_cover_universeLift (X : Scheme.{u})
    {I : Type (u + 1)} (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X)
    (hcover : Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ fpqcPrecoverage X) :
    Presieve.ofArrows (fun i ↦ schemeUniverseLift.{u, u + 1} (U i))
      (fun i ↦ schemeUniverseLiftMap.{u, u + 1} (f i)) ∈
        fpqcPrecoverage (schemeUniverseLift.{u, u + 1} X)
